components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.pinyin: “Duìbuqǐ!” “Méishì, méi guānxi.”
example.english: "Sorry!" "It's fine, no worries."
example.fact: 没事 swings between two almost opposite everyday uses: reassuring someone that a mishap is "no big deal," and describing having free time (我没事, "I'm not busy") — both senses fall out naturally from the same literal meaning, "there is no matter/business going on."

examples.hanzi: 你没事吧？要不要去医院？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ méi shì ba? Yào bu yào qù yīyuàn?
examples.english: Are you okay? Do you need to go to the hospital?

examples.hanzi: 没事，你先忙，我自己来。
examples.pinyin: Méi shì, nǐ xiān máng, wǒ zìjǐ lái.
examples.english: Never mind, you go ahead and be busy; I'll do it myself.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 济 is to ferry across, so to help and relieve.
齐 (qí) — near sound — 济 is jì; 齐 also sounds out 剂 jì and 挤 jǐ.

example.hanzi: 这个国家的经济发展很快。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de jīngjì fāzhǎn hěn kuài.
example.english: This country's economy is developing quickly.
example.fact: 经济 is generally believed to have entered modern Chinese via a Japanese coinage (経済, keizai) that repurposed two Classical Chinese characters — 经 ("to manage, regulate") and 济 ("to aid, benefit") — to translate the Western concept of "economy," one of many modern terms that traveled from Chinese characters to Japan and back again.

examples.hanzi: 学好英语对经济发展也有帮助。
examples.pinyin: Xuéhǎo Yīngyǔ duì jīngjì fāzhǎn yě yǒu bāngzhù.
examples.english: Learning English well also helps economic development.

examples.hanzi: 最近经济不好，很多人找不到工作。
examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn jīngjì bù hǎo, hěn duō rén zhǎo bú dào gōngzuò.
examples.english: The economy is poor lately and many people can't find jobs.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 灬 is fire at the bottom, as in 热, 照, 点; 熟 is cooked food, then ripe and familiar.
孰 (shú) — same sound — 熟 is shú, like 孰.

example.pinyin: Zhège píngguǒ hái méi shú.
example.english: This apple isn't ripe yet.
example.fact: 熟 covers ripe, cooked and familiar: 煮熟 (cook thoroughly), 成熟 (mature), 熟人 (acquaintance), 熟悉 (be familiar with). Conversationally it is often read shóu, as in 饭熟了.

examples.hanzi: 牛肉煮熟了吗?
examples.pinyin: Niúròu zhǔ shú le ma?
examples.english: Is the beef cooked yet?

examples.hanzi: 我和他不太熟悉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé tā bú tài shúxī.
examples.english: I'm not very familiar with him.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 说 say, 问 ask; 告 is "to tell". 告 also gives sound to 造 zào and 靠 kào.

example.pinyin: Wǒ gàosu nǐ yí gè hǎo xiāoxi.
example.english: I have good news to tell you.
example.fact: 告 forms 告诉 (to tell), 报告 (report), 广告 (advertisement), 告别 (to say farewell) and 告状 (to tell on someone). In the legal sense it also means to sue.

examples.hanzi: 电视上有很多广告。
examples.pinyin: Diànshì shang yǒu hěn duō guǎnggào.
examples.english: There are lots of ads on TV.

examples.hanzi: 他向警察报告了情况。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng jǐngchá bàogào le qíngkuàng.
examples.english: He reported the situation to the police.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 检 first meant a wooden label or seal.
佥 (qiān) is a close sound clue for jiǎn; also in 验 yàn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 险 xiǎn.

example.pinyin: Yīshēng yào gěi nǐ zuò jiǎnchá.
example.english: The doctor is going to give you an examination.
example.fact: 检 appears in 检查 (to inspect, to check), 体检 (physical exam), 检验 (to test) and 检讨 (self-criticism). 检查 can be anything from a quick check to a medical examination.

examples.hanzi: 公司每年组织员工体检。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī měi nián zǔzhī yuángōng tǐjiǎn.
examples.english: The company arranges physical exams for staff every year.

examples.hanzi: 请检验一下这些产品。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiǎnyàn yíxià zhèxiē chǎnpǐn.
examples.english: Please inspect these products.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 达 is to get through to, to reach.
大 (dà) is only a loose stand-in for the old sound part, so treat it as a rough clue for dá.
成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.

example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng zhōngyú dáchéng le xiéyì.
example.english: The two sides finally reached an agreement.
example.fact: 达成 almost always takes an abstract object — an agreement, a goal, a consensus (达成协议, 达成目标) — rarely a physical destination, a job usually left to 到达 or 抵达 instead, even though all three share the root 达 ("to arrive at").

examples.hanzi: 我们终于达成了共识。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngyú dáchéng le gòngshí.
examples.english: We finally reached a consensus.

examples.hanzi: 他努力了很久，终于达成了目标。
examples.pinyin: Tā nǔlì le hěn jiǔ, zhōngyú dáchéng le mùbiāo.
examples.english: He worked hard for a long time and finally accomplished his goal.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants, as in 草, 花, 菜; 芝 is a type of plant, like sesame.
之 (zhī) — same sound — 芝 is zhī, like 之.
力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
可 (kě) doubled — a loose sound hint for gē. The same 哥 sounds out 歌 gē (song).

example.hanzi: 他下个月要搬到芝加哥工作。
example.pinyin: Tā xià gè yuè yào bāndào Zhījiāgē gōngzuò.
example.english: He's moving to Chicago for work next month.
example.fact: 芝加哥 is a pure phonetic transliteration: each character (芝 "iris/fungus," 加 "to add," 哥 "elder brother") was chosen only to approximate the English sound, with no attempt at meaning — the standard method Chinese uses for foreign place names with no natural semantic equivalent.

examples.hanzi: 芝加哥的冬天非常冷。
examples.pinyin: Zhījiāgē de dōngtiān fēicháng lěng.
examples.english: Winters in Chicago are very cold.

examples.hanzi: 我们从芝加哥坐火车去了纽约。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen cóng Zhījiāgē zuò huǒchē qù le Niǔyuē.
examples.english: We took a train from Chicago to New York.

components.note: 大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 妇 is a married woman.
彐 (hand) — 彐 is a hand holding a broom (the traditional 婦 had 帚), so a married woman who keeps house.

example.hanzi: 这对夫妇结婚三十年了。
example.pinyin: Zhè duì fūfù jiéhūn sānshí nián le.
example.english: This couple has been married for thirty years.
example.fact: 夫妇 reads a shade more formal and written than the everyday 夫妻, and it almost always pairs with the measure word 对 (一对夫妇, "a couple") rather than 个 — a small detail that underscores a couple being counted as one bonded unit rather than two separate people.

examples.hanzi: 那对夫妇有两个可爱的孩子。
examples.pinyin: Nà duì fūfù yǒu liǎng ge kě'ài de háizi.
examples.english: That couple has two lovely children.

examples.hanzi: 一对年轻夫妇搬进了隔壁。
examples.pinyin: Yí duì niánqīng fūfù bān jìn le gébì.
examples.english: A young married couple moved in next door.

components.note: 广 (building) — 广 is a building or roof, as in 店, 床, 库; 座 is a seat in a hall.
坐 (zuò) — same sound — 座 is zuò, like 坐 (to sit).
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zuòwèi rànggěi lǎorén.
example.english: Please give up your seat for the elderly.
example.fact: 座位 literally joins "seat" (座, a raised place to sit) with "position" (位) — the same 位 that serves as a polite measure word for people (三位客人, "three guests") shows up here instead marking a location, a reminder of how flexibly one character can drift between counting people and naming the spot they occupy.

examples.hanzi: 这个座位有人坐吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhège zuòwèi yǒu rén zuò ma?
examples.english: Is anyone sitting in this seat?

examples.hanzi: 我想订两个靠窗的座位。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng dìng liǎng ge kào chuāng de zuòwèi.
examples.english: I'd like to reserve two seats by the window.

components.note: 子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound) — as in 险, 阳, 阴: a walled yard.
完 (wán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; also in 玩 wán.

example.pinyin: Tā zài yīnyuè xuéyuàn xué gāngqín.
example.english: She studies piano at the music conservatory.
example.fact: 学院 sits a notch below 大学 ("university") in China's usual naming conventions — it typically names a specialized college or faculty (音乐学院, "music conservatory"; 医学院, "medical school") rather than a full university, so translating it simply as "university" can overstate the institution.

examples.hanzi: 他哥哥在一所医学院工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā gēge zài yì suǒ yīxuéyuàn gōngzuò.
examples.english: His older brother works at a medical college.

examples.hanzi: 这个学院有很多外国留学生。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xuéyuàn yǒu hěn duō wàiguó liúxuéshēng.
examples.english: This college has many international students.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — a picture of an ox's head with horns; as a radical it marks cattle, in 牺, 牲, 牧, 物.
女 (woman) — women and relatives: 妈, 姐, 姑; 奶 is milk or a grandmother.
乃 (nǎi) sounds exactly like 奶.

example.hanzi: 我早饭喜欢喝一杯牛奶。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎofàn xǐhuan hē yì bēi niúnǎi.
example.english: I like to drink a glass of milk for breakfast.
example.fact: 牛奶 spells out the animal up front — 牛 ("cow") + 奶 ("milk") — where English "milk" defaults to cow's milk unless stated otherwise; that's why other kinds need their own explicit compound in Chinese, like 羊奶 ("goat's milk") or 豆奶 ("soy milk"), rather than a qualifier added to a generic base word.

examples.hanzi: 我每天早上都喝牛奶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang dōu hē niúnǎi.
examples.english: I drink milk every morning.

examples.hanzi: 冰箱里还有一瓶牛奶。
examples.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ hái yǒu yì píng niúnǎi.
examples.english: There is still a bottle of milk in the fridge.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 逃 is to run away.
兆 (zhào) — loose hint — 逃 is táo; 兆 also sounds out 桃 táo (same sound) and 跳 tiào.
走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.

example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu chènluàn táozǒu le.
example.english: The thief fled in the confusion.
example.fact: 逃走 pairs 逃 ("to flee") with 走, which here works not as its own full verb but as a directional complement meaning "away" — the same role 走 plays in 拿走 ("take away") and 跑走 ("run away"), a common resultative pattern in Mandarin verb compounds.

examples.hanzi: 犯人趁警察不注意逃走了。
examples.pinyin: Fànrén chèn jǐngchá bú zhùyì táozǒu le.
examples.english: The prisoner ran away when the police weren't looking.

examples.hanzi: 小狗从院子里逃走了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu cóng yuànzi lǐ táozǒu le.
examples.english: The puppy escaped from the yard.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — the plant radical, as in 花 flower and 草 grass; it points to crops and harvest, the sense in 收获. Simplified 获 replaces 獲's left side with 艹.
犾 (dog-like part) — a variant of 犬 dog; 獲 originally meant catching game. Memory aid: grass plus a hunting dog, you bring something home.
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; here part of the simplified form 胜 for victory.
生 (shēng) is a near sound match for shèng; also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.

example.pinyin: Zhōngguó duì zài juésài zhōng huòshèng.
example.english: The Chinese team won in the final.
example.fact: 获胜 is distinctly more formal and written than the everyday 赢 ("to win") — it shows up in sports commentary and news headlines, while 赢 dominates casual speech (我赢了, "I won"), a register split worth tracking when choosing between the two.

examples.hanzi: 我们队在比赛中获胜了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duì zài bǐsài zhōng huòshèng le.
examples.english: Our team won the game.

examples.hanzi: 哪一队会获胜，还很难说。
examples.pinyin: Nǎ yí duì huì huòshèng, hái hěn nán shuō.
examples.english: It's hard to say which team will win.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.pinyin: Tā yímiàn zǒulù, yímiàn chàng gē.
example.english: She walked and sang at the same time.
example.fact: 一面's most common job in modern speech isn't "one side" at all, but half of the paired construction "一面...,一面..." ("while... at the same time..."), used to describe two actions happening together — a grammatical use built on the more literal meaning "one face/aspect" of something running alongside another.

examples.hanzi: 这件事要从两方面来看，一面是好处，一面是风险。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yào cóng liǎng fāngmiàn lái kàn, yímiàn shì hǎochu, yímiàn shì fēngxiǎn.
examples.english: This matter has to be viewed from two aspects: one is the benefits, the other the risks.

examples.hanzi: 他一面吃饭，一面看电视。
examples.pinyin: Tā yímiàn chī fàn, yímiàn kàn diànshì.
examples.english: He watches TV while eating.

components.note: 爫 (hand) — a hand 爫 reaching down to a tree 木 to pick its fruit or leaves — to gather, as in 采访.
耳 (ear) — a hand 又 taking an ear 耳: in ancient battle a trophy of capture. Seen in 取得 and in 娶 qǔ, 趣 qù, 最 zuì.

example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ cǎiqǔ le xīn de cuòshī.
example.english: The government adopted new measures.
example.fact: 采取 only ever takes abstract objects like measures, actions, or attitudes (采取措施, "adopt measures"; 采取态度, "take a stance") — it can't mean physically "picking something up," a job left to its component 采 alone (as in 采花, "to pick flowers") or to a plain verb like 拿.

examples.hanzi: 我们必须采取行动保护环境。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū cǎiqǔ xíngdòng bǎohù huánjìng.
examples.english: We must take action to protect the environment.

examples.hanzi: 医生采取了新的治疗方法。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng cǎiqǔ le xīn de zhìliáo fāngfǎ.
examples.english: The doctor adopted a new treatment method.

components.note: 毛 (hair, fur) — hair and fine things: 毯 blanket, 尾 tail; 毫 is fine hair, then a tiny amount, as in 毫米 millimeter.
高 (gāo) is only a loose sound hint for háo.
無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
疋 (foot) — the lower right. Dictionary story: an old man walking 疋 with a cane. Early forms show a person looking around, unsure. Treat as a memory aid.
矢 (arrow) — Dictionary reads it as a cane held by an old man; memory aid: an old man leaning on a stick, unsure which way — doubt, 怀疑.
门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.

example.hanzi: 毫无疑问,他是这次比赛最优秀的选手。
example.pinyin: Háowúyíwèn, tā shì zhè cì bǐsài zuì yōuxiù de xuǎnshǒu.
example.english: Without a doubt, he is the best competitor in this competition.
example.fact: 毫无疑问 is built from 毫 ("the tiniest amount," originally "a fine hair") negated by 无 ("without") plus 疑问 ("doubt, question") — literally "not the slightest hair of doubt," the same intensifying use of 毫 that appears in 毫不 ("not in the least") to negate something as completely as possible.

examples.hanzi: 毫无疑问，这是最好的办法。
examples.pinyin: Háowú yíwèn, zhè shì zuì hǎo de bànfǎ.
examples.english: Without a doubt, this is the best way.

examples.hanzi: 这件事毫无疑问是他的错。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì háowú yíwèn shì tā de cuò.
examples.english: There is no doubt that this was his fault.

components.note: 斤 (axe) — chopping, as in 所, 斩: freshly cut wood is new (薪 xīn is firewood).
亲 (qīn) is a close sound clue for xīn.
女 (woman) — mothers and girls: 妈, 姑, 姐; 娘 is mother or young woman, as in 新娘 bride.
良 (liáng) is a loose sound hint (-iang); same part in 狼 láng and 浪 làng.

example.hanzi: 新娘穿着一件白色的婚纱。
example.pinyin: Xīnniáng chuānzhe yí jiàn báisè de hūnshā.
example.english: The bride is wearing a white wedding dress.
example.fact: 新娘 literally means "new mother/woman" (新 "new" + 娘, an old word for "mother" or young woman) — its counterpart 新郎 ("bridegroom") pairs the same 新 with 郎, an old term for a young man, so the two wedding words are built on matching "new + gendered elder-term" patterns from opposite sides.

examples.hanzi: 新娘今天特别漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Xīnniáng jīntiān tèbié piàoliang.
examples.english: The bride looks especially beautiful today.

examples.hanzi: 新郎和新娘一起切了蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Xīnláng hé xīnniáng yìqǐ qiē le dàngāo.
examples.english: The groom and bride cut the cake together.

components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — the top. Memory aid: grains of rice sorted by size 大 — sorted into groups, a kind (人类). Not proven etymology.
類 (traditional) — used for 'kind, class' with 犬 and 页. 类 is the simplified shape and keeps only a fragment of it.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth, as in 地, 城; a mold was made of clay, so 型 is a model or type.
刑 (xíng) — same sound — 型 is xíng, like 刑.

example.hanzi: 这部电影属于喜剧类型。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng shǔyú xǐjù lèixíng.
example.english: This movie belongs to the comedy genre.
example.fact: 类型 is the more technical, classificatory word for "type" — common in genres, models, and data categories (电影类型, "film genre"; 数据类型, "data type" in programming) — where the plainer, everyday 种 (as in 各种, also in this batch) covers "kind" in casual conversation.

examples.hanzi: 你喜欢哪种类型的音乐？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan nǎ zhǒng lèixíng de yīnyuè?
examples.english: What type of music do you like?

examples.hanzi: 这两个产品类型不同。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge chǎnpǐn lèixíng bù tóng.
examples.english: These two products are of different types.

components.note: 十 (ten/cross) — the visible part; 升 once was a ladle measuring grain, then 'to rise'. The shape does not explain this. Memory aid: a ladle lifted high.

example.pinyin: Tàiyáng cóng dōngfāng shēngqǐ.
example.english: The sun rises in the east.
example.fact: 升 means to rise and is the same character used for 'liter' (一升水). It builds 升级 (to upgrade), 升职 (to be promoted) and 升旗 (to raise a flag). The opposite is 降 (jiàng).

examples.hanzi: 他今年升职了。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīnnián shēng zhí le.
examples.english: He got promoted this year.

examples.hanzi: 今年物价又上升了。
examples.pinyin: Jīnnián wùjià yòu shàngshēng le.
examples.english: Prices have gone up again this year.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 财, 费; 购 is to buy.
勾 (gōu) — near sound — 购 is gòu; 勾 also sounds out 构 gòu and 沟 gōu.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ dǎsuàn qù gòuwù.
example.english: I plan to go shopping this weekend.
example.fact: 购物 is a formal, written-register verb-object compound (购 "to purchase" + 物 "goods") that shows up in signage and compounds like 购物中心 ("shopping mall") — everyday spoken Chinese more often reaches for the plainer 买东西 ("to buy things") to say the same thing.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢在网上购物。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài wǎng shang gòuwù.
examples.english: I like shopping online.

examples.hanzi: 购物前，先列一个清单吧。
examples.pinyin: Gòuwù qián, xiān liè yí ge qīngdān ba.
examples.english: Make a list before you go shopping.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住 live.
旦 (dàn) gives the exact sound; 旦 also sounds out 担 dān and 胆 dǎn.
心 (heart) — wishes and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 愿 is what the heart wants.
原 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; 原 also in 源 yuán.

example.pinyin: Dànyuàn míngtiān shì gè hǎo tiānqì.
example.english: I only wish tomorrow's weather will be good.
example.fact: 但愿 opens a sentence to express a hope for something the speaker can't control or isn't confident about — unlike 希望 ("to hope"), which freely takes a subject and object (我希望你...), 但愿 behaves more like a fixed interjection, closer to English "if only" than to an ordinary verb.

examples.hanzi: 但愿你能早日康复。
examples.pinyin: Dànyuàn nǐ néng zǎorì kāngfù.
examples.english: I hope you get well soon.

examples.hanzi: 但愿一切都顺利。
examples.pinyin: Dànyuàn yíqiè dōu shùnlì.
examples.english: May everything go smoothly.

components.note: 今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.
尸 (body, building) — dwelling and body words: 居, 屋, 层; 属 is to belong to a family or group.
Traditional 屬 had 蜀 (shǔ) as sound part, also in 独 dú, 烛 zhú, 触 chù; simplified 属 keeps the reading shǔ.

example.pinyin: Zhè bǎ yǐzi shì jīnshǔ zuò de.
example.english: This chair is made of metal.
example.fact: 金's modern default sense has narrowed toward specifically "gold" (金子) in most everyday compounds — 金属 preserves the character's older, broader meaning by adding 属 ("category, class"), literally "the metal category," so the general sense of "metal" survives alongside the newer, narrower one.

examples.hanzi: 金属很容易导电。
examples.pinyin: Jīnshǔ hěn róngyì dǎo diàn.
examples.english: Metal conducts electricity easily.

examples.hanzi: 这个杯子是用金属做的，不怕摔。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bēizi shì yòng jīnshǔ zuò de, bú pà shuāi.
examples.english: This cup is made of metal and won't break if dropped.

components.note: 纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (silk), as in 红, 给; colours come from dyed silk.
录 (lù) — same sound — 绿 is lù (lǜ in colour), like 录.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan chuān lǜsè de yīfu.
example.english: She likes wearing green clothes.
example.fact: 绿 is one of the relatively few Mandarin syllables that requires the umlaut ü, written lǜ — since lu and lü are distinct syllables in Pinyin (English "u" has no such counterpart), learners typing without an ü key, or simply mishearing the vowel, often garble it as "lu4" instead.

examples.hanzi: 春天来了，树叶都变成了绿色。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān lái le, shùyè dōu biàn chéng le lǜsè.
examples.english: Spring has come and the leaves have all turned green.

examples.hanzi: 绿色的蔬菜对身体好。
examples.pinyin: Lǜsè de shūcài duì shēntǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Green vegetables are good for your health.

meanings: variant of 抽菸|抽烟[chou1 yan1]

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 抽 is to pull out.
由 (yóu) — near sound — 抽 is chōu; 由 also sounds out 油 yóu and 邮 yóu.
火 (fire) — 火 is fire, as in 烧, 灯, 炒; 烟 is smoke.
因 (yīn) — near sound — 烟 is yān; 因 also sounds out 姻 yīn.

example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā búyào chōuyān.
example.english: The doctor advised him not to smoke.
example.fact: 抽烟 literally means "to draw/pull smoke" (抽 "to pull out" + 烟 "smoke") — the same verb 抽 used for drawing a card from a deck (抽签) or drawing water up from a well, here applied to pulling smoke into the lungs.

examples.hanzi: 他以前每天抽烟，现在已经戒了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǐqián měi tiān chōuyān, xiànzài yǐjīng jiè le.
examples.english: He used to smoke every day but has now quit.

examples.hanzi: 请问，这里可以抽烟吗？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, zhèlǐ kěyǐ chōuyān ma?
examples.english: Excuse me, is smoking allowed here?

meanings: to take part in an election

components.note: 立 (stand) — traditional 競 shows two people standing side by side in competition; 竞 keeps 立 and one 兄.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.

example.pinyin: Tā juédìng jìngxuǎn shìzhǎng.
example.english: He decided to run for mayor.
example.fact: 竞选 combines 竞 ("to compete, contend") with 选 ("to select, elect") — literally "to compete to be selected" — and it almost always takes the office being sought directly as its object (竞选总统, "to run for president"), with no preposition needed the way English inserts "for."

examples.hanzi: 她打算明年竞选班长。
examples.pinyin: Tā dǎsuàn míngnián jìngxuǎn bānzhǎng.
examples.english: She plans to run for class monitor next year.

examples.hanzi: 两位候选人正在竞选总统。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng wèi hòuxuǎnrén zhèngzài jìngxuǎn zǒngtǒng.
examples.english: Two candidates are running for president.

components.note: 合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.pinyin: Zhège jiàgé hěn hélǐ.
example.english: This price is very reasonable.
example.fact: 合理 literally means "fitting with reason" (合 "to fit, match" + 理 "reason, logic"); its opposite 不合理 ("unreasonable") is formed by simply adding 不 in front — one of several everyday adjectives built directly on 理 ("logic, principle"), alongside 道理 ("sense, reason") and 理论 ("theory").

examples.hanzi: 你的要求很合理。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de yāoqiú hěn hélǐ.
examples.english: Your request is very reasonable.

examples.hanzi: 请合理安排你的时间。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng hélǐ ānpái nǐ de shíjiān.
examples.english: Please arrange your time sensibly.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 检 first meant a wooden label or seal.
佥 (qiān) is a close sound clue for jiǎn; also in 验 yàn, 剑 jiàn, 脸 liǎn and 险 xiǎn.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water: 河, 深, 浅; 测 was measuring the depth of water.
则 (zé) is close to cè; same part in 侧 cè and 厕 cè.

example.hanzi: 医院对样本进行了检测。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn duì yàngběn jìnxíng le jiǎncè.
example.english: The hospital tested the sample.
example.fact: 检测 leans technical and instrument-based — lab tests, medical screenings, sensor readings (病毒检测, "virus testing") — where its near-synonym 检查 covers the broader everyday sense of "to check, inspect," like checking luggage or homework, a split that roughly maps onto English "to detect" versus "to check."

examples.hanzi: 机场正在检测每位旅客的体温。
examples.pinyin: Jīchǎng zhèngzài jiǎncè měi wèi lǚkè de tǐwēn.
examples.english: The airport is testing every traveler's temperature.

examples.hanzi: 这台机器可以检测空气质量。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái jīqì kěyǐ jiǎncè kōngqì zhìliàng.
examples.english: This machine can detect air quality.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室; 完 first meant complete, whole.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; 元 also sounds out 玩 wán, 院 yuàn and 远 yuǎn.
虫 (insect, creature) — small animals and insects, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake, 虾 shrimp: 蛋 is the egg of a creature.

example.hanzi: 如果考试再不及格,我就完蛋了。
example.pinyin: Rúguǒ kǎoshì zài bù jígé, wǒ jiù wándàn le.
example.english: If I fail the exam again, I'm done for.
example.fact: 完蛋 is a colloquial idiom, not a literal statement about eggs — 完 ("finished") plus 蛋 ("egg") together evoke something "cracked, done for, ruined," in the same register as English slang "cooked" or "toast"; it's casual and best avoided in formal writing.

examples.hanzi: 完蛋了，我把钥匙锁在车里了！
examples.pinyin: Wándàn le, wǒ bǎ yàoshi suǒ zài chē lǐ le!
examples.english: I'm done for; I locked my keys in the car!

examples.hanzi: 要是老板知道了，我们就完蛋了。
examples.pinyin: Yàoshi lǎobǎn zhīdào le, wǒmen jiù wándàn le.
examples.english: If the boss finds out, we're done for.

components.note: 月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.
门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.

example.hanzi: 春节期间,很多商店都不营业。
example.pinyin: Chūnjié qījiān, hěn duō shāngdiàn dōu bù yíngyè.
example.english: During the Spring Festival period, many stores are closed.
example.fact: 期间 almost always attaches after another noun to mean "during [that period]" (春节期间, "during Spring Festival"; 假期期间, "during the holiday") rather than standing alone as a general word for "time" — for that broader sense, Chinese reaches for 时间 instead.

examples.hanzi: 暑假期间，我在一家咖啡店打工。
examples.pinyin: Shǔjià qījiān, wǒ zài yì jiā kāfēidiàn dǎgōng.
examples.english: During summer vacation, I work part-time at a coffee shop.

examples.hanzi: 在这期间，你有什么问题可以问我。
examples.pinyin: Zài zhè qījiān, nǐ yǒu shénme wèntí kěyǐ wèn wǒ.
examples.english: During this time, you can ask me any questions you have.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 舟 is a boat, as in 船, 般; 航 is sailing.
亢 (kàng) — near sound — 航 is háng; 亢 also sounds out 抗 kàng and 坑 kēng.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — a blade 刂 cutting two jades apart: to divide into groups, hence class or shift.

example.hanzi: 我们的航班延误了两个小时。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de hángbān yánwù le liǎng gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: Our flight was delayed two hours.
example.fact: 航班 specifically names a scheduled flight identified by a number (航班号, "flight number") — for the general idea of air travel or the aircraft itself, Chinese uses 飞机 or 航空, reserving 航班 strictly for the scheduled-service sense, closer to English "flight 205" than to "airplane."

examples.hanzi: 这个航班几点起飞？
examples.pinyin: Zhège hángbān jǐ diǎn qǐfēi?
examples.english: What time does this flight take off?

examples.hanzi: 因为大雾，所有的航班都取消了。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi dàwù, suǒyǒu de hángbān dōu qǔxiāo le.
examples.english: Because of heavy fog, all flights were canceled.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun radical — dark is the lack of daylight; compare 明 bright, 晚 evening.
音 (yīn) — loose sound hint — 暗 is àn; 音 also sounds out 谙 ān.

example.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ hěn àn.
example.english: It is very dark in the room.
example.fact: 暗 is dark in the sense of dim light: 黑暗 (darkness), 昏暗 (gloomy). It also means hidden or secret: 暗示 (to hint), 暗恋 (to have a secret crush). 黑 (hēi) is more about color black.

examples.hanzi: 天暗了,该回家了。
examples.pinyin: Tiān àn le, gāi huíjiā le.
examples.english: It's getting dark; time to go home.

examples.hanzi: 他暗暗下定了决心。
examples.pinyin: Tā àn'àn xiàdìng le juéxīn.
examples.english: He secretly made up his mind.

components.note: 白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 他今天穿了一件白色的衬衫。
example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān chuān le yí jiàn báisè de chènshān.
example.english: He wore a white shirt today.
example.fact: Beyond the color itself, 白色 carries a historical political charge: 白色恐怖 ("White Terror") describes state violence against leftist movements, following the same international convention — also used for the "White" forces in the Russian Civil War — of pairing white with anti-revolutionary factions, as the opposite of red's association with communism.

examples.hanzi: 白色的墙让房间看起来更大。
examples.pinyin: Báisè de qiáng ràng fángjiān kàn qǐlái gèng dà.
examples.english: White walls make the room look bigger.

examples.hanzi: 冬天，山上到处都是白色的雪。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān, shān shang dàochù dōu shì báisè de xuě.
examples.english: In winter, the mountains are covered in white snow.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.pinyin: Tā xīnzhōng chōngmǎn le gǎnjī.
example.english: Her heart was filled with gratitude.
example.fact: 心中 literally means "inside the heart" (心 "heart" + 中 "middle, inside") and reads as a more literary, introspective way to say "in one's heart/mind" — its plainer everyday counterpart is 心里, built the same way but with 里 ("inside") in place of 中.

examples.hanzi: 他心中一直有一个梦想。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīnzhōng yìzhí yǒu yí ge mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: He has always had a dream in his heart.

examples.hanzi: 我心中很清楚该怎么做。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīnzhōng hěn qīngchu gāi zěnme zuò.
examples.english: I know very well in my mind what I should do.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫; 嘴 is a mouth or lips.
觜 (zuǐ) — same sound — 嘴 is zuǐ, like 觜.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.pinyin: Tā zuǐlǐ hánzhe yí kuài táng.
example.english: He had a piece of candy in his mouth.
example.fact: 嘴里 extends past its literal "inside the mouth" to describe reported speech, as in 从他嘴里听说的 ("heard it from him") — treating the mouth as the source of words, a metonymy that also shows up in the more formal, literary 口中, built on 口 (the classical word for mouth) instead of the everyday 嘴.

examples.hanzi: 别嘴里含着东西说话。
examples.pinyin: Bié zuǐ lǐ hán zhe dōngxi shuō huà.
examples.english: Don't talk with food in your mouth.

examples.hanzi: 她嘴里一直念着我的名字。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuǐ lǐ yìzhí niàn zhe wǒ de míngzi.
examples.english: She kept murmuring my name.

components.note: 广 (building) — marks halls and shelters, as in 店, 座, 床; 库 is a storehouse, here for carts 车.

example.pinyin: Huòwù dōu fàng zài cāngkù lǐ.
example.english: The goods are all kept in the warehouse.
example.fact: 库 is a store for things: 仓库 (warehouse), 车库 (garage), 水库 (reservoir), 库存 (inventory). It also names digital storage, as in 数据库 (database) and 题库 (question bank).

examples.hanzi: 车库里停着两辆车。
examples.pinyin: Chēkù li tíng zhe liǎng liàng chē.
examples.english: Two cars are parked in the garage.

examples.hanzi: 这些数据存在数据库里。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shùjù cún zài shùjùkù li.
examples.english: This data is stored in the database.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁; 镇 first meant to weigh down with metal.
真 (zhēn) — near sound — 镇 is zhèn; 真 also sounds out 慎 shèn and 填 tián.

example.pinyin: Zhège xiǎozhèn fēngjǐng hěn měi.
example.english: This small town has beautiful scenery.
example.fact: 镇 names a specific level in China's administrative hierarchy — below a county (县) but above a village (村) — so 小镇 isn't just a vague descriptor but points to a real category of town-level unit, a more precise use than how loosely English "small town" tends to get applied.

examples.hanzi: 这个小镇只有一条街。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎozhèn zhǐyǒu yì tiáo jiē.
examples.english: This small town has only one street.

examples.hanzi: 我在一个安静的小镇长大。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài yí ge ānjìng de xiǎozhèn zhǎng dà.
examples.english: I grew up in a quiet little town.

components.note: 生 (birth) — traditional 產 was 生 (birth) topped by 彦 for sound; the idea is giving birth, so bringing forth, as in 生产 and 产生.
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 这家公司的产品质量很好。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de chǎnpǐn zhìliàng hěn hǎo.
example.english: This company's products are of great quality.
example.fact: 产品 joins 产 ("to produce") with 品 ("item" — itself three stacked 口 "mouth" components, suggesting many voices judging or discussing something) to give the neutral business term for anything manufactured, distinct from 商品, which specifically emphasizes an item as merchandise bought and sold.

examples.hanzi: 这个产品很受年轻人欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chǎnpǐn hěn shòu niánqīng rén huānyíng.
examples.english: This product is very popular with young people.

examples.hanzi: 我们公司刚推出了一款新产品。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī gāng tuīchū le yì kuǎn xīn chǎnpǐn.
examples.english: Our company just launched a new product.

components.note: 米 (rice) — refined grain gives the idea of essence and the best part, hence 精 fine, spirit (精神).
青 (qīng) is a near sound match (-ing); the series 青 清 请 情 晴 静 helps recall jīng.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.pinyin: Niánqīngrén jīnglì chōngpèi.
example.english: Young people are full of energy.
example.fact: 精力 refers specifically to a person's physical or mental stamina — the energy to get through a task or a day — while the physics sense of "energy" (kinetic, electrical) uses the unrelated word 能量 instead, a distinction easy to miss since English "energy" covers both.

examples.hanzi: 照顾孩子要花很多精力。
examples.pinyin: Zhàogù háizi yào huā hěn duō jīnglì.
examples.english: Taking care of children takes a lot of energy.

examples.hanzi: 我今天没有精力再工作了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān méiyǒu jīnglì zài gōngzuò le.
examples.english: I don't have the energy to work anymore today.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 退 is to step back.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住, 做.
木 (tree) — a person 亻 leaning on a tree 木: resting, hence 休息 rest and 退休 retire.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yéye qùnián tuìxiū le.
example.english: My grandfather retired last year.
example.fact: 退休 literally means "to withdraw and rest" (退 "to withdraw, retreat" + 休 "to rest") — 休 is itself a picture of a person 亻 leaning against a tree 木, giving the word an almost literal image of stepping back to finally relax after a working life.

examples.hanzi: 他明年就要退休了。
examples.pinyin: Tā míngnián jiù yào tuìxiū le.
examples.english: He is going to retire next year.

examples.hanzi: 退休以后，爷爷喜欢养花。
examples.pinyin: Tuìxiū yǐhòu, yéye xǐhuan yǎng huā.
examples.english: After retiring, grandpa likes to grow flowers.

components.note: 兵 (soldier) — old forms show two hands (the 八 at the bottom) holding an axe (the top, now written 丘), so weapons in hand means soldier.

example.pinyin: Tā zài jūnduì dāng bīng.
example.english: He serves as a soldier in the army.
example.fact: 兵 means soldier: 当兵 (join the army), 士兵 (soldier), 骑兵 (cavalry). 兵马俑 is the name of the Terracotta Army figurines, and 纸上谈兵 is an idiom about 'discussing war only on paper'.

examples.hanzi: 士兵们在操场上训练。
examples.pinyin: Shìbīngmen zài cāochǎng shang xùnliàn.
examples.english: The soldiers are training on the field.

examples.hanzi: 他刚退伍,以前是个老兵。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāng tuìwǔ, yǐqián shì ge lǎobīng.
examples.english: He just left the army; he used to be a veteran soldier.

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: hidden indoors, secret.
宓 (mì) gives the exact sound; also in 蜜 mì.

example.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ guānxì hěn qīnmì.
example.english: The two of them have a very close relationship.
example.fact: 亲密 describes emotional closeness between people (亲密关系, "intimate relationship") — worth not confusing with the visually similar 亲近 (a milder word for growing familiarity) or 亲自 ("in person, personally"), which despite looking related has nothing to do with closeness at all.

examples.hanzi: 这两个孩子从小就很亲密。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge háizi cóngxiǎo jiù hěn qīnmì.
examples.english: These two children have been close since they were little.

examples.hanzi: 他们是亲密的朋友，什么都可以说。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì qīnmì de péngyou, shénme dōu kěyǐ shuō.
examples.english: They are close friends and can talk about anything.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and worship: 神 god, 祝 wish, 福 fortune; 礼 are ritual courtesies.
豸 (beast) — 豸 is an animal or beast radical, as in 豹; 貌 is appearance.
皃 (mào) — same sound — 貌 is mào, like 皃.

example.pinyin: Gēn zhǎngbèi shuōhuà yào yǒu lǐmào.
example.english: You should be polite when speaking with elders.
example.fact: 礼貌 combines 礼 ("ritual, etiquette," built on the altar/spirit radical 礻, tied to formal ceremony) with 貌 ("appearance, looks") — literally something like "the outward form of proper conduct," which is why 有礼貌 ("polite," lit. "having politeness") treats good manners as a visible quality one possesses.

examples.hanzi: 孩子要学会有礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Háizi yào xuéhuì yǒu lǐmào.
examples.english: Children need to learn to be polite.

examples.hanzi: 他对客人很有礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì kèrén hěn yǒu lǐmào.
examples.english: He is very polite to guests.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 这座城市有一个地下停车场。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu yí gè dìxià tíngchēguǎn.
example.english: This city has an underground parking garage.
example.fact: 地下 extends from its literal "below ground" sense to anything secret or operating outside official channels — 地下工作 ("underground work," covert political activity) and 地下经济 ("underground economy") borrow the same spatial metaphor English uses for "underground" resistance or black markets.

examples.hanzi: 地下的水管坏了，需要修理。
examples.pinyin: Dìxià de shuǐguǎn huài le, xūyào xiūlǐ.
examples.english: The underground water pipe is broken and needs repair.

examples.hanzi: 我家在地下一层有一间储藏室。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài dìxià yì céng yǒu yì jiān chǔcángshì.
examples.english: My home has a storage room on the basement level.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 胡 first meant the flesh hanging under the chin.
古 (gǔ) — near sound — 胡 is hú; 古 also sounds out 湖 hú and 糊 hú.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.pinyin: Bié húshuō, zhè búshì zhēn de.
example.english: Don't talk nonsense, that's not true.
example.fact: 胡 in 胡说 traces back to an old, disparaging term for non-Han peoples of Central Asia (as in 胡人) — that historical sense of "foreign, other, hence wild or unruly" survives in several unrelated-looking compounds like 胡乱 ("carelessly, haphazardly") and 胡闹 ("to act foolishly, make a scene").

examples.hanzi: 你别胡说，我没有那样说过。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié húshuō, wǒ méiyǒu nàyàng shuō guo.
examples.english: Stop talking nonsense; I never said that.

examples.hanzi: 他喝醉了，一直在胡说八道。
examples.pinyin: Tā hēzuì le, yìzhí zài húshuō bādào.
examples.english: He was drunk and kept spouting nonsense.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
朋 (friend) — oldest form shows two strings of cowrie shells (old money) side by side; they paired up and came to mean companions.
又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.

example.hanzi: 他是我的老朋友,我们认识二十年了。
example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de lǎo péngyou, wǒmen rènshi èrshí nián le.
example.english: He's my old friend — we've known each other for twenty years.
example.fact: 老 prefixed onto a word for a person doesn't necessarily describe age — it signals long-standing familiarity instead (老同学, "old classmate"; 老同事, "old colleague"), so even two twenty-year-olds can call each other 老朋友. Separately, dictionaries also record 老朋友 as an established colloquial euphemism for a menstrual period — the same two characters carrying a completely different, informal sense.

examples.hanzi: 今晚我要和几个老朋友吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn wǒ yào hé jǐ ge lǎo péngyou chī fàn.
examples.english: Tonight I'm having dinner with a few old friends.

examples.hanzi: 老朋友来了，我们聊了一个晚上。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo péngyou lái le, wǒmen liáo le yí ge wǎnshang.
examples.english: An old friend came, and we chatted all evening.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 挥 is to wave or wield.
军 (jūn) — near sound — 挥 is huī; 军 also sounds out 辉 huī.

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài zhǐhuī jiāotōng.
example.english: The police officer is directing traffic.
example.fact: 指挥 does double duty as both a verb ("to direct, command") and a noun ("conductor, commander") — the same word covers directing traffic, commanding troops, and conducting an orchestra. 指 contributes "finger, to point" and 挥 contributes "to wave, swing (the hand)," building a fairly literal picture of hand gestures for directing others.

examples.hanzi: 他在乐队里负责指挥。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yuèduì lǐ fùzé zhǐhuī.
examples.english: He is in charge of conducting in the orchestra.

examples.hanzi: 船长正在指挥大家搬东西。
examples.pinyin: Chuánzhǎng zhèngzài zhǐhuī dàjiā bān dōngxi.
examples.english: The captain is directing everyone to move things.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — 弓 as in 张, 弯, 弹 — characters of stretching and drawing; 强 is about strength like a strong bow.
丬 (bed) — near sound — 壮 is zhuàng; 丬 also sounds out 状 zhuàng and 装 zhuāng.
士 (scholar, man) — 士 is a man, as in 战士; 壮 is a strong man.

example.hanzi: 他身体很强壮,每天都锻炼。
example.pinyin: Tā shēntǐ hěn qiángzhuàng, měitiān dōu duànliàn.
example.english: He's physically strong — he exercises every day.
example.fact: 强壮 specifically describes physical robustness of a body, person or animal — unlike 强 alone, which can also describe abstract strength (国力强, "national power is strong"). Pairing 强 with 壮 (built from 士, "soldier") narrows the meaning down to bodily sturdiness.

examples.hanzi: 他长得又高又强壮。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de yòu gāo yòu qiángzhuàng.
examples.english: He is tall and strong.

examples.hanzi: 多运动，身体才会强壮。
examples.pinyin: Duō yùndòng, shēntǐ cái huì qiángzhuàng.
examples.english: Exercise more and your body will become strong.

components.note: 刂 (knife; 刀) — marks cutting, as in 别 separate, 刻 carve, 划 slice; 割 is cutting, as with a knife or sickle.
害 (hài) — loose sound hint (gē vs hài).

example.pinyin: Tā yòng dāo gēkāi le shéngzi.
example.english: He cut the rope with a knife.
example.fact: 割 is cutting with a sweeping stroke, such as reaping or slicing: 收割 (harvest), 割草 (mow grass). 割舍 means to give up something dear, and 割肉 is also stock-market slang for selling at a loss.

examples.hanzi: 农民在田里割麦子。
examples.pinyin: Nóngmín zài tián li gē màizi.
examples.english: The farmers are cutting wheat in the field.

examples.hanzi: 他不小心割伤了手。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn gēshāng le shǒu.
examples.english: He accidentally cut his hand.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
力 (strength) — 力 is strength, as in 办, 动, 努; 劲 is energy and force.
又 (hand) — 又 here stands in for the older 巠, which gave the near sound: 经 jīng, 轻 qīng.

example.hanzi: 你今天看起来不太对劲,还好吗?
example.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān kàn qǐlai bú tài duìjìn, hái hǎo ma?
example.english: You seem a bit off today — are you okay?
example.fact: 对劲 overwhelmingly appears negated as 不对劲 ("something's not right, off") in everyday speech — the bare positive 对劲 is comparatively rare and can sound slightly incomplete on its own, a pattern shared by a handful of Chinese words that live mostly in their negative form.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子今天有点不对劲，是不是病了？
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi jīntiān yǒudiǎn bú duìjìn, shì bu shì bìng le?
examples.english: This child seems off today; is he sick?

examples.hanzi: 我们俩说话总是不对劲。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen liǎ shuō huà zǒngshì bú duìjìn.
examples.english: The two of us never get along well when we talk.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 他变化很大,但我还是认出他了。
example.pinyin: Tā biànhuà hěn dà, dàn wǒ háishi rènchū tā le.
example.english: He's changed a lot, but I still recognized him.
example.fact: The 出 after 认 doesn't mean "to exit" here — as a verb complement it marks succeeding at pulling something out of memory or out of a crowd, the same "figure it out" sense of 出 found in 查出 (also in this batch, "to find out") and 想出 ("to think up, to figure out").

examples.hanzi: 我一眼就认出了他。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yì yǎn jiù rènchū le tā.
examples.english: I recognized him at a glance.

examples.hanzi: 你能认出这是哪个字吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng rènchū zhè shì nǎge zì ma?
examples.english: Can you tell which character this is?
